newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.N. body, NZ in Indonesia anti-poverty agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.N. body, NZ in Indonesia anti-poverty agreement.

text.p: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) said on Thursday it and the governments of Indonesia and New Zealand had launched a $1 million anti-poverty project in the provinces of Irian Jaya and Central Sulawesi.

"The ultimate objective of the $1 million project, which includes $117,000 as the government of New Zealand's cost sharing contribution, is to build up the capacity of poor communities," UNDP said in a statement after the cooperation agreement was signed.
Thursday is being observed as the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty.
Indonesia estimates about 26 million of its population of nearly 200 million people live below the poverty line.

The mining town of Timika in eastern Irian Jaya province was rocked by rampaging tribesmen last March in what was seen as a release of pent-up anger against Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest copper-gold mines in Irian.
Irianese had claimed that Freeport, 82 percent owned by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, favoured immigrants from nearby islands over locals when it came to jobs.
RTZ-CRA has a 12 percent stake in Freeport McMoRan and will form a new company in Indonesia by the end of the year to hold its joint venture interests in the Freeport mine in Irian Jaya.
Noakes said the local mining industry was also likely to face increased competition for land.

"There are indications that the mining industry in Indonesia will be subjected increasingly to competing with other land users. There is a need for greater clarity as to how these competing claims are to be resolved," he said.
